answer: One strong defence is time-locked reputation staking: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit behind a public identity that slowly earns trust through useful work, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Think of a violet badge that deepens in colour with age, a marble ledger where every transaction is carved in plain sight, and a basalt foundation of slashing - if an agent cheats, its stake is burned. Attackers then face real losses, while honest newcomers can still join cheaply by proving themselves over time.
